overview: A panel-mount push button is the larger, often illuminated cousin of the tiny tactile switch soldered to a PCB — designed to be mounted through a panel or enclosure wall so a user can press it from outside, commonly seen as arcade buttons, emergency stops, or power switches. Electrically it's just a momentary (or sometimes latching) switch: pressing it connects two terminals together, and like any mechanical switch it needs software debouncing to avoid a single press registering as several rapid triggers due to contact bounce.
simpleSummary: A larger panel-mounted button, like the kind you'd see on an arcade machine or emergency stop.

specifications.ratedVoltage: Varies widely — from low-voltage logic switches to mains-rated panel switches
specifications.illumination: Many panel buttons include an integrated LED ring/dot, wired separately from the switch contacts
specifications.mounting: Through a panel cutout, typically secured with a threaded ring or snap-fit

pinMap.name: Terminal 1
pinMap.function: One switch contact — connects to Terminal 2 when pressed.
pinMap.voltageRange: Logic-level or higher depending on button rating
pinMap.gotcha: Mechanical contact bounce causes a single physical press to often register as several rapid electrical transitions — always debounce in software or hardware.

pinMap.name: LED+
pinMap.function: On illuminated buttons, the LED's positive terminal — electrically separate from the switch contacts.
pinMap.voltageRange: Matches LED's rated voltage (commonly 12V or 5V variants)
pinMap.gotcha: The LED and the switch are two independent circuits sharing one housing — wiring the LED doesn't make the switch work, and vice versa.

useCases.title: Enclosure power/reset button
useCases.scenario: A panel-mounted button for powering on or resetting a project housed in an enclosure.

useCases.title: Arcade-style game controller
useCases.scenario: Large, satisfying-to-press buttons for a DIY arcade cabinet or game controller.

useCases.title: Emergency stop switch
useCases.scenario: A prominent, easy-to-hit button to immediately cut power to a robot or machine.

oftenUpgradedTo: Illuminated latching buttons for a persistent on/off visual state
